q: 1. If the average compressive strength is 4000 kg/cm² and standard deviation is 500, coefficient of variation is
explain: Coefficient of variation = (Standard deviation / Mean) × 100 = (500/4000) × 100 = 12.5%.

q: 2. Workability of concrete is measured by
explain: The slump test is the standard field and lab method used to measure the consistency/workability of fresh concrete.

q: 3. Specified compressive strength of concrete is obtained from cube tests at the end of
explain: By convention and IS code practice, the characteristic/specified compressive strength of concrete is defined based on 28-day cube test results, by which time hydration has developed most of the strength.

q: 4. Allowable shear strength of concrete depends on
explain: The allowable/permissible shear strength used in design is derived directly from the concrete's own shear strength characteristics as established by codes.

q: 5. ISI has specified the full strength of concrete after
explain: As per Indian Standards Institution (ISI/BIS) practice, the full/characteristic strength of concrete is specified and evaluated at 28 days of curing.

q: 6. The increase in the strength of concrete with time is
explain: Concrete strength gain over time follows a non-linear curve — rapid initially and gradually slowing down, not a straight line.

q: 7. The test conducted in the laboratory on the specimen made out of trial concrete mix is called
explain: A preliminary test is conducted in the laboratory on trial mixes before actual construction to determine and verify the proportions needed to achieve the required strength.

q: 8. The strength of concrete after one year as compared to 28 days strength is about
explain: Continued hydration over time increases strength beyond the 28-day value; typical long-term gain at one year is about 20-25% more than the 28-day strength.

q: 9. Modulus of rupture of concrete is a measure of
explain: Modulus of rupture is obtained from a flexure (bending) test on a concrete beam and represents its flexural tensile strength.

q: 10. Poisons ratio for concrete
explain: As per this text, Poisson's ratio of concrete tends to increase as the mix becomes richer (higher cement content).

q: 11. 1% of voids in concrete mix would reduce its strength by about
explain: As a general rule of thumb used in concrete technology, each 1% of entrapped air voids reduces compressive strength by approximately 5%.

q: 12. Minimum grade of concrete to be used in RCC as per IS 456: 1978 is
explain: As per the (older) IS 456:1978 provisions referenced here, M10 was permitted as the minimum grade usable in reinforced cement concrete.

q: 13. For concreting of heavily reinforced sections without vibration, the workability of concrete expressed as compacting factor should be
explain: Heavily reinforced sections placed without mechanical vibration need a very high workability mix; the compacting factor required in such cases is above 0.92.

q: 14. The individual variation between test strength of sample should not be more than
explain: As per the code check on scatter of test results, the maximum permitted variation of an individual sample strength from the average is ±5% of the average value.

q: 15. The ratio of various ingredients in concrete of grade M20 is
explain: M20 grade concrete corresponds to the nominal mix proportion of 1:1.5:3 (cement:fine aggregate:coarse aggregate) as per traditional nominal mix classification.

q: 16. The approx. ratio of the direct tensile strength to direct compressible strength test is
explain: The direct tensile strength of concrete is generally only about 1/10th (0.10) of its direct compressive strength, reflecting concrete's inherent weakness in tension.

q: 17. The concrete mix which is not amicable for smooth finish is said to posses
explain: A harsh concrete mix — one with excessive hardness/harshness due to insufficient fines or paste — is difficult to finish smoothly.

q: 18. In concrete mix design, allowance for bulking of sand is necessary in case of
explain: Bulking changes the apparent volume of sand due to moisture, so a correction is required only when proportioning is done by volume (volume batching), not by weight.

q: 19. Di-calcium silicate (C2S)
options: provides less ultimate strength to cement
has less resistance to soleplate attack
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and, correspondingly, releases less heat of hydration compared to tricalcium silicate.

q: 20. In concrete mix design, allowance for surface water carried by aggregate is necessary in case of
explain: Surface moisture on aggregate adds extra water to the mix and affects the effective water-cement ratio regardless of whether batching is done by volume or by weight, so an allowance is needed in both cases.

q: 21. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The degree of grinding of cement, is called fineness
The process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement.
The phenomenon by virtue to which cements does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement.
The heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as neat of hydration.
explain: This statement is incorrect: soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to resist volume expansion/change after setting, not to sound transmission — the two share a similar-sounding name but different meanings.

q: 22. Water required for M25 concrete per bag of cement, is
explain: As per the standard nominal mix proportioning tables referenced in this text, the water requirement per 50 kg bag of cement for M25 grade concrete is taken as 35 kg.

q: 23. The compressive strength of concrete determined from 150 mm × 150 mm cylinder as compared to that determined from 150 mm cube is
explain: Cylinder specimens generally record lower compressive strength than cube specimens of comparable size due to differences in the stress distribution and end-restraint effects during testing.

q: 24. The continuous strain which the concrete undergo due to application external loadsis called
explain: Creep is defined as the gradual, time-dependent increase in strain in concrete under sustained (constant) external load.

q: 25. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: Harshness (difficulty in placing/finishing) in a concrete mix occurs when there is a deficiency of fines and an excess of coarser particles relative to the mix design.

q: 26. The grade of concrete M 150 means that compressive strength of 15 cm cube after 28 days, is
explain: The grade designation M150 directly indicates that the characteristic compressive strength of a 15cm cube after 28 days of curing is 150 kg/cm².

q: 27. According to I.S. : 456, the number of grades of concrete mixes, is
explain: As per IS:456, concrete mixes were historically classified into 7 grades based on specified compressive strengths (though modern codes list more, this classic reference lists 7).

q: 28. The preliminary test is repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimens, exceeds
explain: If the compressive strength results of three specimens from a preliminary test vary by more than 15 kg/cm², the test is considered unreliable and must be repeated.

q: 29. The ratio of various ingredients (cement, sand, aggregates) in concrete of grade M20, is
explain: The nominal mix proportion traditionally associated with grade M20 concrete is 1 : 1.5 : 3 (cement : sand : coarse aggregate).

q: 30. The 28 days cube strength of mass concrete using aggregates of maximum size 5 cm for gravity dams should be
explain: Mass concrete for gravity dams using 5cm maximum size aggregate is typically specified to achieve a 28-day cube strength ranging between 150 to 500 kg/cm².

q: 31. The approximate ratio of direct tensile strength to direct compressive strength test of concrete
explain: Concrete is inherently weak in tension compared to compression; its direct tensile strength is only about 1/10th (approximately 0.10) of its direct compressive strength.

q: 32. The concrete in which preliminary tests are performed for designing the mix is called
explain: Controlled concrete is that for which preliminary trial mixes and tests are conducted to design and control the exact proportions for target strength.

q: 33. The maximum quantity of aggregates per 50 kg of cement should be
explain: As per the arbitrary/nominal mix guidance in this text, the maximum permissible quantity of aggregate per 50 kg bag of cement is about 450 kg.

q: 34. The minimum quantity of cement to be used in controlled concrete is specified is
explain: For controlled concrete mix design, the minimum cement content specified in this text is 220 kg per cubic metre.

q: 35. The concrete in which no preliminary tests are performed for designing the mix is called
explain: Ordinary concrete uses fixed nominal mix proportions without preliminary trial-mix testing, unlike controlled concrete.

q: 36. The ordinary concrete is not used for ......... grade of concrete mix.
explain: Ordinary (nominal mix) concrete is limited to lower/moderate grades; high-strength grades such as M40 require controlled mix design and are not made using ordinary concrete practice.

q: 37. The controlled concrete is used for
explain: Controlled concrete mix design is applicable across the full range of seven grades of concrete specified in the code.

q: 38. For reinforced cement concrete lintels and slabs, the nominal size of coarse aggregate should not exceed.
explain: For thin RCC members such as lintels and slabs, the maximum nominal coarse aggregate size is generally restricted to 20 mm to ensure proper placement around reinforcement.

q: 39. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of cement warehouse is
explain: As per warehouse construction guidance in this text, the concrete floor thickness for a cement storage warehouse should not exceed about 15 cm.

q: 40. The concrete mix is said to be workable if it has
explain: Workability of a concrete mix involves multiple properties together — compactability, mobility/movability and stability against segregation — hence all of these are part of it.

q: 41. For the improvement of workability of concrete, the shape of aggregate recommended is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and interparticle friction, improving the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 42. The steel mould used for slump test is in the form of
explain: The slump test mould is a hollow frustum of a cone (truncated cone) shape, open at both ends, as standardized in IS 1199.

q: 43. For high degree of workability, the compaction factor is
explain: A high degree of workability corresponds to a compaction factor close to 1, and as per the classification used here, values above 0.92 (option 0.95) represent high workability.

q: 44. Proper proportioning of concrete, ensures
explain: Correct mix proportioning of cement, aggregates, and water ensures all these desirable properties - strength, workability, durability, water tightness, and wear resistance - together.

q: 45. As the grade of concrete increases the quantity of cement required per cubic metre
explain: Higher grade concrete requires higher compressive strength, which is generally achieved by increasing the cement content per cubic metre of concrete.

q: 46. Allowable shear strength of concrete, depends upon
explain: The allowable (permissible) shear strength value used in design is directly based on the concrete's own inherent shear strength characteristics.

q: 47. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following. While performing preliminary test on concrete
options: proportions of the material and water should be the same as to be used at the work site
cement should be mixed by hand in order to maintain uniformity
concrete mix should be stored in air-tight containers
concrete ingredients should be kept at a temperature of 37 deg +/- 2 deg C
explain: For preliminary tests, mixing should ideally be done as it would be at the site (usually by machine, not hand) to reflect actual site conditions; mixing by hand purely 'to maintain uniformity' is not the correct requirement, making this statement incorrect.

q: 48. Minimum number of test specimens required for finding the compressive strength of concrete are
explain: As per standard practice, a minimum of 3 test specimens (cubes) are cast and tested to determine the compressive strength of a concrete batch.

q: 49. The preliminary test is repeated if the difference of compressive strength of three test specimens, exceeds
explain: If the range (difference) between the highest and lowest strength values of the three specimens exceeds 15 kg/cm², the test results are considered unreliable and the preliminary test must be repeated.

q: 50. For the construction of R.C.C. slabs, columns, beams, walls, etc. the grade of concrete mix used, is
explain: A nominal mix of 1:2:4 (cement:sand:aggregate), corresponding to M15 grade, is commonly used for general R.C.C. work such as slabs, beams, and columns.
